City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
April 10, 2018
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:00 p.m. , on April 10, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on January 01, 1, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Mayor Sachs
Mayor Pro Tem Raths
Council Member Goodell
Council Member Kelley
Absent:
Council Member Bucknum
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Conference with Legal Counsel-Existing Litigation: Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9; Name of case: Webster et al vs. City of Mission Viejo.
CS2.
Conference with Real Property Negotiators - Government Code Section 54956.8: Property: Mission Viejo Village Center: Agency Negotiator, City Manager, Community Development Director, City Attorney: Negotiating Parties; HWA DAH LLC, The Patio in Mission Viejo, Trojan Sports LLC, Jann Gath, La Paz Viejo Company LLC, OC Generations V Limited Partnerships, 413 Adams Street Associates, Russell E. Fluter, Thomas Family Partners-Mission Viejo, Todd I. Schiffman, and MV Village Properties LLC.
CS3.
Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are the City and Cityâ€™s Unrepresented Employees. The Cityâ€™s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
CS4.
Conference with Legal Counsel â€“ Anticipated Litigation: Significant Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) or (3) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 â€“ Threat of Litigation From City of Santa Ana to Compel Homeless Management, Support or Housing.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Bucknum was absent).
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were four Closed Session matters and in all cases, the Council received updates and provided direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.
INVOCATION: Council Member Raths
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
State Legislative Update
Cory Williams from Townsend Public Affairs presented the legislative update.
P2.
Update on California WaterFix and Regional Water Reliability
The City Council received the presentation from Drew Atwater, Director of Planning for Moulton Niguel Water District.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Carole Weidler, M.V.: grand reopening of the MAC was more than awesome. Not enough adjectives give the grand opening justice, trumpeters in tuxedos on the dive platform, Greg diving, Brian taking the first lap. Entire facility is amazing and first class. Final result is completely commensurate with the cost. Commended staff. Liaison for CDS and was thrilled to see CDS residents there.
The following expressed opposition to the shooting of rabbits in the Palmia community: Joanne Cashman, M.V.; C.J. Reagan, M.V.; Wayne Ferguson, M.V.; and Jeannie Kruchten, M.V.
Rand Johnson, M.V.: announced that he has been serving Orange County as a mobile locksmith for over 30 years and he thanked the City for its business.
The following expressed concern with the proposal to change the hours of OCFA 911 dispatchers: Jon Dumitru, Orange; Megan Soman, San Juan Capistrano; Chad Kurthy, Rancho Santa Margarita.
Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Saturday entering the Nadadores Wendy Bucknum chastised her for attending the MAC grand re-opening but Kim Barnes welcomed her. world renowned organization is heavily subsidized by the MV taxpayers.
Jason Yi, M.V.: representing the Community of Character Committee, he announced that the character word for the month of April is "service" and he described attributes and careers surrounding service. Character film on Sunday April 15 "The Longest Day."
Inhee Carter, M.V.: expressed concern with dry brush and camping, encampments in the Wilderness Glen area. Neighbors are worried about the potential for fires and asked the Council to consider instituting a park curfew to help address the situation.
Ryan Farsai, M.V.: stated that the City placed an electronic marquee on his property behind the ARCO station on Marguerite and La Paz.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Item 4 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the Consent Calendar as outlined below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Mayor Sachs, Mayor Pro Tem Raths, Council Member Goodell, and Council Member Kelley
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Bucknum
1.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of March 27, 2018, as presented.
2.
Check Register Dated March 17, 2018 in the Amount of $1,349.367.54
Ratified the accompanying check register.
3.
Check Register Dated March 23, 2018 in the Amount of $2,496,513.97
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
Traffic Signal Maintenance-Contract Change Order 3
Approved Contract Change Order 3 with Computer Service Company in an amount not to exceed $129,182.00.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
4.
2017 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 18838)-Notice of Completion
Kelley said that Council received a note today from a resident who submitted a concern.
Chagnon responded that the resident commented on a slurry seal project that was completed in 2017. He said the slurry is cracking and is not up to par and shouldn't have been accepted. Changon noted that slurry is meant to seal and hold a street until an asphalt overlay is done and some level of cracking on slurry is acceptable.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1) certify the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and (4) authorize payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Mayor Sachs, Mayor Pro Tem Raths, Council Member Goodell, and Council Member Kelley
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Bucknum
STAFF REPORTS
6.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update from Chief Capobianco
Chief Capobianco presented the report.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
7.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Bucknum
Council Member Goodell
Congratulations to Dennis, KEith and all of the staff for a beautiful job well done for the MAC. Phenomenal and never imagined that that facility would look that great. Grand opening event was fun and wonderful to see all the residents and families out celebrating Saturday. So appreciative of the support that has been shown to the Nadadores and it was fun for him to take the "first swim" in the pool. Thanked staff for a job well done. Also attended Coach Rose's retirement party Fri night and it was wonderful to celebrate with him and thank him for his service to the community. Ad hoc committee has been meeting a good group of people have been working hard to think of different avenues to reach out to the world and bring in programs. Promote our city as an Olympic city where people can come train and compete. Engaging with the Nadadores, Saddleback College and reaching out to our own recreation department and others who are very excited about the possibilities ahead of us with all of the facilities re-opening. Things to do to enhance and increase our exposure to the world as an Olympic city.
Council Member Kelley
Kelley, outlined attendance at recent events including Bunny Days, commended organizers and volunteers who help make that possible. 5 month old granddaughter picture was taken with the Easter Bunny. Grand re-opening of MAC was spectacular. The beauty of the facility, uniqueness of the new dive tower and every detail of the finished product is state-of-the-art, world class and the event itself was phenomenal. Thanked city staff for the team effort to present the event. Volunteer appreciation lunch, very impressive event as well. Room was filled with people who volunteer, really wonderful event and celebration. Upcoming events, Sat April 21 Earth Day/Arbor Day a time to plant and work to provide volunteer efforts. 8 to noon at Cordova Park; mark your calendars for Arts Alive, April 28 and 29. Do not want to miss it. Thanked Jason Ye for presenting at the beginning of the meeting and presenting the word of the month, service. discussed how the program documents are provided to the schools and she discussed traits that describe the word "service."
Mayor Pro Tem Raths
Shout out to Dave Leckness one of the P&T Commissioner and editor of the privately owned newspaper "The Reporter." He wrote an article complimenting him for what he has done. Included his phone number and 100% of the calls have all been very positive about the city. Very pleased with the aquatics center and the park renovations going on. Elks club representative attended and thanked the Elks for all they do for the community, and providing scholarships and awards for students and seniors. Rotary Club, annual fundraiser this Saturday, entertainment night and Texas Hold 'Em tournament... all money goes to local charities. Visit MV Rotary website shows the charities that are being supported and you can choose one.
Mayor Sachs
8.
Mayor's Quarterly Report
Tomorrow he is attending an SRO meeting and excited to attend and listen to some of the things that will be discussed and an opportunity to discuss his Secure OC Schools initiative and lay out some of the things they'll be doing and how important the SROs are in that initiative. During public comments, park curfews, can we agendaize them or learn about the city's current laws. Pleasure of going to the OC Airport fire station which is operated by the County and he had the opportunity to ride on the brand new crash truck during a mock exercise with a small plane.
Provided an update on his goals for the first quarter of 2018.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 8:35 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, April 24, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.
